mustFixFindings.narrowReadingRefuted: Two narrow readings were tested and both fail. (a) 'The remeasurementClause exempts append-only COORD growth, so a lagging pin is licensed.' The growth is indeed strictly append-only - c61d668f is a byte-exact 1090395-byte prefix of the live 1103108-byte COORD, verified by hashing the live file's first 1090395 bytes - so that clause is not itself violated. But the clause reads 'If a cited file moves in a way that is not append-only COORD growth or COORD heading hygiene ... remasure before recording': it is a forward-looking drift rule telling a later recorder when a file that moves AFTER the pin forces remeasurement. It does not license recording, at authoring time, a COORD state that predates the artifact's own declared head. Here the growth preceded authoring - D-336 and D-337 were already in COORD when the subject was written at a7937c57 - so nothing about the exemption reaches this defect. (b) 'COORD is not a subject of this cycle, so its pin need not move.' rejectionStatement: g21 leftover-join.v18 is an otherwise clean and surgical remeasurement. Its delta against dual-ACCEPT g21 leftover-join.v17 removes nothing, adds 41 leaves and changes 55, of which only 17 are substantive after rename normalization, and every one of those 17 is a correct consequence of D-336 and D-337: D-335 is properly demoted out of last-heading custody, corpus v16 is properly demoted from current to predecessor first-authoring, the current-remasurement pointer is properly re-aimed at g21 leftover-join.v17 (D-336), and the four D-337 copies are properly remasured stale as an authoring claim in five places. 94 of 94 path/digest pairs, 17 of 17 commit pins, and 60 of 60 cited review verdicts re-resolve true against live bytes. The four fixture payloads are byte-exact. leftoverDesign correctly remains [OBL-G21-FX-AUTHORING], leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded is correctly [], both frozen unrecorded predecessors keep their Findings-land tails intact, no identifier is coined for the unlabeled Codex finding, and there is no deixis. It is rejected on a single omission in the one field that records what it measured. $.recordedInputs['docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md'] was inherited from v17 byte-for-byte while $.recordedInputs.HEAD beside it advanced two recordings, so the artifact pins COORD as of D-335 while declaring itself measured at D-337. The pinned bytes contain neither D-336 nor D-337. That leaves the subject's sole last-heading claimant, its D-336 current-remasurement pointer, and the D-337 trigger that is this cycle's entire reason for existing, all unverifiable from the artifact's own evidence record - and it makes the artifact disagree with itself about when it was measured. Every prior version in this lineage, v1 through v17, kept the COORD pin equal to COORD at its own head. The remedy is one digest.
